summary: Fort Chipewyan Airport (YPY) serves the remote community of Fort Chipewyan in northeastern Alberta, located near the western shore of Lake Athabasca. As one of the oldest European-established communities in Alberta, the airport is a critical transportation lifeline since the town has no permanent road access to the rest of the province, relying instead on seasonal ice roads, barges, and air travel. It primarily accommodates regional turboprop flights connecting residents to Fort McMurray and other northern destinations.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly into Fort Chipewyan Airport?
A: Charter and regional carriers serve YPY, with flights typically connecting to Fort McMurray operated by smaller turboprop aircraft suited to the remote airfield.

Q: How do you get to Fort Chipewyan?
A: The community has no all-weather road access; travel is by air year-round, supplemented by barge service on Lake Athabasca in summer and a seasonal winter ice road.

Q: Is Fort Chipewyan Airport paved?
A: The airport has a paved runway, though its remote location means weather conditions and seasonal factors can affect flight schedules.

Q: How far is the airport from the town centre?
A: The airport is located a short drive from Fort Chipewyan's community centre, making passenger transfers relatively quick.
transport_tips: Ground transport options at the airport are limited, so arranging a shuttle or pickup with your hotel or host in advance is strongly recommended. Taxis may be available but are not guaranteed, especially during off-peak hours. Renting a vehicle locally is uncommon due to the absence of connecting roads to other communities.
local_tip: Pack extra layers even in summer—Fort Chipewyan sits well north of the prairies and experiences cool temperatures and biting insects, especially near the lake and surrounding boreal forest.
